result: The existing full smoke passed on the exact fixed candidate 9777b84/8b3a239 with class=software (SwiftShader). Default entry stayed v10 and advanced (tick 12->18); candidate v11 passed real player move/stop, targeting, effect, hero selection, key remap, and Save match -> reload -> Continue saved match (savedTick 27 -> resumedTick 37, Q remapped to F); the diffuse sidecar loaded with stylized-diffuse lighting. Bot hero id 10 (team 1) advanced 14.467 units over 62 ticks (tick 13 -> 75) toward its moveGoal while the player hero stayed at spawn, from a post-run read-only snapshot observation; run.mjs itself does not directly assert bot position/advance, so that bot result is not a runner assertion. All console/page/http/request gates and cleanup arrays were empty; browser exit 0 and the preview port closed. History/exit addendum (history-exit-notes.json): the 14.467 observation and a review-phase reproduction are separate read-only calls with their own call identifiers and times, but their browser process exit codes were not captured and the original smoke's exit 0 is not applied to them. The two prior Git head.exe -30 filters were each produced by one of two grep|head -30 pipelines issued by the prior tower unit's implement subagent at 02:35:37Z; both were local_bash calls that hit their 120 s timeout at 02:37:37Z and continued in the background, and both belong to that prior unit rather than this one. One matched the prior tower unit's registered process-subtree creation-time window; the other came from the second call and its parent chain was not registered. Both were present in the 03:30Z census and both are absent from the 04:39:43Z census; neither has an exit receipt, so both exit times/codes are unknown; no lock was cleared. The fixed-source smoke and 37-file hash match stay usable for delivery; the unknown exits block only subsequent local serial scheduling.
